Container.Name: OppaiLib
Container.Overview: OppaiLib — a private, self-hosted, encrypted media library for adult content (videos, GIFs, images, comics, and game entries) with tagging, URL scraping, and fully local AI auto-tagging. Also includes Libby, an in-app chat companion with importable character cards, which talks to an OpenAI-compatible LLM you run yourself. Everything stays on your box: no cloud storage, no cloud AI, no telemetry.
Container.Description: Self-hosted encrypted NSFW media library. Set a strong master passphrase — it encrypts all stored media and CANNOT be recovered if lost.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Web interface / API port

Config.Name: Media (encrypted store)
Config.Description: Encrypted blob storage

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Keystore and site parsers. The AI model ships inside the image at /opt/oppailib/models and is not stored here.

Config.Name: Database
Config.Description: SQLite metadata database. Keep this on a local pool (an SSD cache share) rather than on an SMB/NFS mount: a network filesystem cannot support WAL mode, and without WAL every database query in the container queues behind every other one. Settings → Diagnostics says which mode it actually came up in.

Config.Name: Cache (uploads and scratch)
Config.Description: Upload staging and processing scratch. Regenerable — deleting it while the container is stopped costs unfinished uploads and nothing else — but NOT small: a resumable upload holds the whole file here until it is stored, so uploading a 12 GB video needs 12 GB here. Leave this unmapped and it grows inside the Docker image allocation instead, which is the usual cause of "image is full" on a box that uploads video. Settings → Storage shows what is on it.

Config.Name: Libby's memories (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Her memory store, bond, mood, outfits and identity references — by default inside /config. Map this and set OPPAI_LIBBY_DIR to /libby to put the data you would least like to lose on its own share. Stop the container and copy /config/libby across before switching, or she starts from nothing.

Config.Name: Character data (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Imported character cards and their artwork — by default inside /config. Set OPPAI_CHARACTER_DIR to /characters to use it; copy /config/characters across first.

Config.Name: Chat workspaces (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. Conversations, your profile and the images shared into chat — by default inside /config. Set OPPAI_CHAT_DIR to /chat to use it; copy /config/chat across first.

Config.Name: Processing scratch (optional)
Config.Description: Optional. ffmpeg frames, archives being built, AI tagger stills — by default inside /cache. Set OPPAI_TEMP_DIR to /scratch to put it on a fast pool separate from upload staging. Anything left here is deleted automatically once it is older than the window in Settings → Storage.

Config.Name: Libby memory path
Config.Description: Set to /libby only if you mapped the optional Libby memories path above. Blank keeps her memories inside /config, which is where they already are.

Config.Name: Character data path
Config.Description: Set to /characters only if you mapped the optional character path above.

Config.Name: Chat workspace path
Config.Description: Set to /chat only if you mapped the optional chat path above.

Config.Name: Scratch path
Config.Description: Set to /scratch only if you mapped the optional scratch path above. Blank puts scratch inside /cache.

Config.Name: Master Passphrase
Config.Description: Encrypts all media. SAVE THIS — losing it means losing your library. Leave blank on first run to have one generated (check the logs).

Config.Name: Admin Username
Config.Description: First-run admin account

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: First-run admin password

Config.Name: AI Auto-tagging
Config.Description: Enable local AI auto-tagging

Config.Name: AI Device
Config.Description: cpu or cuda (cuda needs GPU passthrough and a CUDA build of libonnxruntime; falls back to cpu with a warning)

Config.Name: AI Video Frames
Config.Description: Frames sampled per video/GIF before merging their tags (capped at 32). Each frame costs one ffmpeg decode plus one inference, so raising this makes video tagging slower but more thorough.

Config.Name: Scrape Delay (ms)
Config.Description: Politeness delay between scraper requests

Config.Name: Respect robots.txt
Config.Description: Honor robots.txt before fetching. Set to false only for a site you own or are authorized to archive, when Fetch returns 'blocked by robots.txt'.

Config.Name: Chat LLM URL
Config.Description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint for Libby chat — LM Studio, llama.cpp, Ollama's /v1 bridge, or text-generation-webui. Example: http://192.168.1.10:5000/v1 . Blank disables chat (Libby falls back to built-in local replies). Chat becomes ready once that API reports a loaded model; load models in its own UI.

Config.Name: Chat Model
Config.Description: Optional fallback model name, for chat servers that require a model field in the request.

Config.Name: Chat API Key
Config.Description: Optional. Needed only when your chat server was started with an API key (e.g. text-generation-webui's --api-key).

Config.Name: Text-generation models (optional)
Config.Description: Optional, and only needed if you want to DELETE text-generation models from OppaiLib's UI — that backend exposes no delete API, so it has to be a file operation. Point this at the same host folder text-generation-webui loads its models from, then set the matching path (/textgen-models) in Settings → Libby. Leave both blank and the delete controls simply do not appear. Deleting moves a model to a recoverable .oppailib-trash folder inside this directory unless you explicitly ask for a permanent delete, and it will never touch the model that is currently loaded.

Config.Name: Image Generation URL
Config.Description: Local image generator for the Create tab: an InvokeAI server (default port 9090) or Automatic1111 / SD.Next (the /sdapi/v1 flavour, default port 7860). Which API it speaks is detected automatically. Blank disables the feature. Also settable at runtime in Settings.

Config.Name: Web Idle Timeout (minutes)
Config.Description: How long a browser session may sit unused before it is signed out. Browser sessions are also signed out whenever the container restarts. The Android app is exempt from both — it stays signed in. Set to 0 to disable the idle timeout.

Config.Name: Session Lifetime (hours)
Config.Description: How long a signed-in session stays valid before requiring a fresh sign-in. Applies to the Android app as well as browsers.
